title: Ross Gerber Questions Tesla's Optimus Bet: 'There's No Revenue Coming Anytime Soon'

Investor Ross Gerber of investment firm Gerber Kawasaki said Elon Musk could face a long road to turning Tesla Inc.'s Optimus into a commercial success, saying humanoid robots remain difficult to build and are unlikely to generate revenue anytime soon.

Human Hands, Feet And Eyes Remain A Challenge

Gerber said the biggest hurdle for humanoid robots was replicating the physical capabilities that make humans unique.

"God was pretty good at making humans over millions of years of evolution. Hands are tough, feet are tough, and eyes are tough," Gerber said in an interview with The Information.

He added that robots using wheels, tracks and other systems have historically been easier to build than machines designed to walk like humans.

.@GerberKawasaki thinks Elon Musk is going to have a hard time building humanoid robots.

"God was pretty good at making humans over millions of years of evolution. Hands are tough. Feet are tough, and eyes are tough. And these are the three things that really make us special… pic.twitter.com/G9MgZ2mIdh

— The Information (@theinformation) July 23, 2026

Gerber Questions Near-Term Revenue

Gerber also questioned the commercial opportunity for consumer-focused humanoid robots, saying the level of investment does not match the near-term revenue potential.

"Spending a trillion dollars to build a robot to fold clothes doesn't make any sense to me at all," he added.

Gerber said that military, space, and industrial applications made more sense, but said Tesla was "spending a lot of money, and there's no revenue coming anytime soon."

Tesla Continues To Bet Big On Optimus

Earlier this month, Musk called the humanoid robot the company's "biggest product of all time," while Tesla began converting factory space in Fremont, California, for Optimus production.

Musk said China will be Tesla's biggest competitor in humanoid robotics, while the company continues testing Optimus internally and plans to ramp production as development progresses.

Wall Street Bets Big on Humanoids

Morgan Stanley estimates the global humanoid robot market could eventually reach about $5 trillion by 2050, while Goldman Sachs forecasts the industry could reach roughly $38 billion by 2035 as advances in artificial intelligence accelerate commercialization.

投资公司格柏川崎 (Gerber Kawasaki) 的投资者罗斯·格柏 (Ross Gerber) 表示，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 要将特斯拉公司的擎天柱 (Optimus) 转化为商业成功，可能面临漫长的道路，他表示，人形机器人仍然难以制造，而且不太可能很快产生收入。

人类的手、脚和眼睛仍然是一个挑战

格伯表示，人形机器人的最大障碍是复制人类独特的身体能力。

“上帝在数百万年的进化过程中非常善于创造人类。 手是艰难的，脚是艰难的，眼睛也是艰难的，”格伯在接受《信息报》采访时说道。

格柏质疑近期收入

格伯还质疑以消费者为中心的人形机器人的商业机会，称投资水平与近期收入潜力不匹配。

“花一万亿美元建造一个折叠衣服的机器人对我来说根本没有任何意义，”他补充道。

格伯表示，军事、太空和工业应用更有意义，但他表示，特斯拉“花了很多钱，而且短期内不会有收入”。

特斯拉继续在擎天柱上押下重注

本月早些时候，马斯克称这款人形机器人是公司“有史以来最大的产品”，而特斯拉则开始改造位于加利福尼亚州弗里蒙特的工厂空间，用于擎天柱的生产。

马斯克表示，中国将成为特斯拉在人形机器人领域的最大竞争对手，而该公司将继续在内部测试 Optimus，并计划随着开发的进展而提高产量。

华尔街在类人机器人上押下重注

摩根士丹利估计，到 2050 年，全球仿人机器人市场最终可能达到约 5 万亿美元，而高盛预测，随着人工智能的进步加速商业化，到 2035 年该行业可能达到约 380 亿美元。
